entities.name: Syria–Lebanon campaign
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Syria–Lebanon campaign, code-named Operation Exporter, was a pivotal Allied invasion of Vichy French-controlled Syria and Lebanon during World War II. 

 The campaign began on June 8, 1941, and lasted for six weeks, resulting in the defeat of the Vichy French forces and the establishment of a British protectorate over the region. 

 The campaign was significant not only for its military outcome but also for its strategic implications, as it secured a vital supply line to the Soviet Union and paved the way for the Allied victory in the Middle East. 

 The campaign's legacy can be seen in the modern-day borders of Lebanon and Syria, as well as the ongoing tensions between the two countries and their respective allies.
